concept: two small stick people rallying a shuttlecock
viewpoint: side view, left player facing right, right player facing left
action: Two small stick figures, about 8-12 cells tall, stand parked in the left fifth and right fifth of the canvas, rallying one shuttle over a low anchored net at center. The left player has just hit: the shuttle is already off the left racket and flying toward the right, still in the left-center, while the right player waits with racket drawn back. The shuttle crosses the long empty middle and the right player swings into a contact key where the shuttle touches the right racket in the right-center — this contact is a key because interpolation cannot invent it. After contact, the shuttle flies back toward the left, slightly higher, while the right player follows through and the left player lifts the racket to receive. Both players stay planted; only arms, rackets, and the shuttle move. The shuttle is the star: a tiny diamond or short dash that makes the long travel while the people stay small at the edges. One shared anchored ground line, one anchored net, no third person, no court lines.
layout_notes: left player in the left fifth, right player in the right fifth, net anchored at center with one low post and short horizontal tape, shuttle travels the long empty middle; ground line shared across the bottom third

parts.name: left player head
parts.notes: round circle head, same size every key, faces right

parts.name: left player torso
parts.notes: short vertical line, stays planted in left fifth

parts.name: left player legs
parts.notes: two short legs touching ground, planted

parts.name: left racket arm
parts.notes: arm lifts from follow-through to ready receive

parts.name: left racket
parts.how: short grip plus small oval head
parts.notes: grip in fist, small oval face, not a sword, angle changes with arm

parts.name: right player head
parts.notes: round circle head, same size every key, faces left

parts.name: right player torso
parts.notes: short vertical line, stays planted in right fifth

parts.name: right player legs
parts.notes: two short legs touching ground, planted

parts.name: right racket arm
parts.notes: swings from back position into contact, then follow-through

parts.name: right racket
parts.how: short grip plus small oval head
parts.notes: grip in fist, small oval face, angle must change start to contact to follow-through

parts.name: shuttlecock
parts.notes: the star; tiny, never a second head; long travel across the middle

parts.name: net
parts.how: one low post plus short horizontal tape
parts.notes: center, copied exactly on every key

parts.name: ground
parts.notes: shared by both players, exact same points every key

keys.name: start
keys.left: left fifth, planted, arm in follow-through after the hit, racket angled up-right
keys.right: right fifth, planted, racket drawn back and up, ready, not yet on the shuttle path
keys.shuttle: just off the left racket, in the left-center, flying right

keys.name: contact
keys.left: left fifth, planted, arm settling from follow-through, racket easing to neutral
keys.right: right fifth, planted, swung into the hit, racket meeting the shuttle in the right-center
keys.shuttle: touching the right racket face in the right-center
keys.notes: contact key, interpolation cannot invent this

keys.name: return
keys.left: left fifth, planted, racket lifted to receive, arm raised
keys.right: right fifth, planted, follow-through, racket swung across after the hit
keys.shuttle: flying back left and a bit higher, in the left-center heading toward the left player

gaps.why: shuttle travels the long middle from left-center to the right racket; right arm swings in during the same interval
shuttle returns the same long distance and slightly higher arc, similar speed, same ease as the inbound half
